rationale: The registered read-index follow-up is written and verified locally, so it is filed rather than left in the draft. The harness elects node 1 with the append acknowledgement withheld, queues a read request (no read state, commit 10), lets the node's own quorum check demote it (StateFollower, term unchanged, still no read state), lets it lead again at term 3 and replicates, so that the new term's commit reaches 12, and then completes the release heartbeat round trip: the stale request is answered there with read index 12 and the original context. Four comparisons carry the question - no read state while the node owes the request but is not leader, the demotion attributed to the node's own check rather than a peer's higher term, the released index being the one at release time rather than the stale acceptance index, and the request-context identity - and all are expected to hold, since the source reading predicted exactly this and it is a permitted, not a defective, outcome.

scope.description: Eighth test function in the same harness file: a leader is elected between two real RawNodes with the append acknowledgement withheld, a read request is queued, the leader is demoted by its own quorum check while nothing is delivered, it is re-elected at a higher term and replicates so that a commit in that term happens, and the release heartbeat round trip is completed to see whether the stale request is answered.
assumptions: The delivery helper writes each Ready's HardState and Entries to the node's storage before Advance, as the Ready contract requires.
Voters are {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with CheckQuorum+PreVote; the leader wins with its own vote plus node 3's, and node 2 is never contacted, so quorum is exactly two.
ReadOnlyOption is the default ReadOnlySafe, so a released request is confirmed by a heartbeat round trip.
While the node is not leader no message from a quorum reaches it, which is what lets its own check end its leadership.
excluded: Wall-clock timing and transport behaviour; only logical ticks and in-process delivery are used.

experiment.prefix: Elect node 1 with the append acknowledgement withheld, issue a ReadIndex request and emit the node's state, term, commit and read states; then tick the node until its own quorum check fires and emit the demoted state with its read states; then campaign again, deliver the votes, emit the renewed leadership with its commit, replicate in a bounded loop until the new term's entry is committed, deliver the release heartbeats to the follower, feed its responses back and emit the released read states with their index and context.
experiment.responsibility: The raft module owns when an accepted read request is answered, and the application owns writing Ready entries to storage before their messages are sent.

comparisons.description: No read state is produced for a request the node still owes while it is not leader, which is the unanswered half of the question.
Attribution: the demotion happened at the term the node led at, so its own quorum check ended the leadership rather than a peer's higher term.
Late completion: the request is answered with the index committed at release time, not the index recorded when it was accepted, so the late answer is not stale.
Identity: the released read state carries the context of this request, so the answer is attributable to it.
